projects.title: Starline: A Time-Bucketed Event Aggregation API That Stays Fast at Millions of Rows
projects.pitch: Rebuild GitHub's star-history lesson from scratch. Seed Postgres with tens of millions of synthetic 'star' events across repos with skewed popularity. Build three versions of a /history endpoint: naive OFFSET/LIMIT pagination, aggregate-then-paginate, and index-range-filter-then-group. Then add a fourth version with incremental daily rollups. Measure each with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and a load generator so you can see exactly where the database does wasted work.
you_will_learn: Why OFFSET/LIMIT still scans skipped rows, and keyset pagination as the alternative
Composite and covering index design for (repo_id, created_at) range scans
Reading query plans: Index Only Scan vs Bitmap Heap Scan vs Seq Scan
Pre-aggregation and rollup tables, including incremental maintenance and late-arriving events
Handling hot keys and skew when one repo has 100x more rows than the median
milestones: Generate a Zipf-distributed dataset of 50M events with a seed script
Implement the naive paginated endpoint and record p50/p99 latency and rows read for small vs huge repos
Add an index-range-filter-before-GROUP-BY version and compare plans with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
Add a daily rollup table maintained by a trigger or batch job, and handle backfills correctly
Write a short benchmark report with charts showing requests and rows touched per approach

projects.title: Replayr: Capture and Replay Real Postgres Traffic Against a New Version
projects.pitch: Write a Postgres wire-protocol proxy that sits between an app and its database. It records every query with its parameters, session and timing into a compact log. A replayer then re-issues that workload against a target database (a new major version, a different index set, or a migrated schema) at 1x, 5x or as-fast-as-possible speed. Finally, diff the latency distributions and result checksums between the two runs.
you_will_learn: Implementing a binary network protocol proxy: startup, simple and extended query flows
Preserving session ordering and transaction boundaries while replaying concurrently
Time-scaling a workload while respecting causal dependencies between queries
Comparing latency histograms (HDR) and detecting regressions statistically
Handling non-determinism in replays, such as now(), sequences and random()
milestones: Build a transparent TCP proxy that forwards traffic and logs raw messages
Parse simple and extended query protocol messages and write structured capture records
Build a replayer that maintains per-session ordering with configurable speed multipliers
Add result checksumming and an HDR-histogram latency diff report between source and target
Use it to catch a real regression, such as a dropped index or a planner change between PG versions

projects.title: AgentVCS: A Content-Addressed Store for Many Agents Editing One Repo Concurrently
projects.pitch: Coding agents now run 5-10 at a time against the same codebase. Build a small versioned file store designed for that load. It uses content-addressed blobs and trees, a compare-and-swap ref update API for optimistic concurrency, and automatic 3-way merge with conflict surfacing. Every agent operation goes into an append-only operation log, so any agent's work can be audited or rolled back. Stress it with a swarm of simulated agents making overlapping edits.
stack: SQLite (WAL mode) or Pebble for refs and op log
you_will_learn: Content addressing, Merkle trees and structural sharing between versions
Optimistic concurrency control with CAS on refs, and retry/backoff under contention
Linearizability of ref updates vs eventual consistency of blob replication
3-way merge, conflict detection and operation logs as an audit and undo mechanism
Garbage collection of unreachable objects without racing live writers
milestones: Implement a blob/tree/commit object model with BLAKE3 hashing and a local object store
Add a ref store with atomic compare-and-swap updates and an append-only op log
Implement automatic 3-way merge on CAS failure, returning structured conflicts
Write a load harness with 20 simulated agents editing overlapping files, and measure conflict rate and throughput
Add mark-and-sweep GC that is safe with concurrent writers, plus an 'undo agent X' command driven by the op log

projects.title: TraceGraph: An Ontology-Backed Knowledge Graph for Root-Cause Analysis
projects.pitch: Build a mini version of Netflix's ontology-driven observability. Run a toy microservice system (5-8 services, a queue and a DB) instrumented with OpenTelemetry. Stream spans, metrics and deploy events into a typed knowledge graph with entities such as Service, Endpoint, Host, Deployment and Dependency. Then write a root-cause query: given a latency regression on one endpoint, walk the graph to rank upstream suspects using recent deploys and error-rate deltas.
you_will_learn: Designing an ontology: entity types, relationship types and identity resolution across telemetry sources
Deriving service dependency graphs from distributed traces
Separating high-cardinality raw telemetry (columnar store) from low-cardinality topology (graph store)
Sampling strategies (head vs tail) and how they bias what the graph can see
Graph traversal heuristics for root-cause ranking, and evaluating them against injected faults
milestones: Stand up the toy service mesh with OTel tracing exporting to the collector
Build an ingestion job that upserts entities and edges into the graph and raw spans into ClickHouse
Model deploy events and config changes as first-class graph nodes linked to services
Implement a root-cause query that ranks suspects by graph distance, error delta and deploy recency
Inject 10 faults with toxiproxy (latency, errors, bad deploy) and measure top-1/top-3 accuracy

projects.title: FleetSim: Resumable OTA Updates and Staged Rollouts for 100k Flaky Virtual Devices
projects.pitch: Simulate a fleet of 100,000 battery-powered IoT sensors as lightweight goroutines. Each one has intermittent connectivity, an energy budget, and A/B firmware partitions. Build the server side to match: chunked, resumable firmware downloads with integrity checks, and staged rollouts (1% → 10% → 100%) that halt automatically when device health telemetry regresses. Partition swap and rollback must happen on boot failure. The control plane has to survive thundering herds when whole stores come back online at once.
you_will_learn: Resumable transfers with chunk manifests, range requests and per-chunk hashing
Backpressure and admission control when 100k devices reconnect simultaneously
Jittered exponential backoff and why it prevents synchronized retry storms
Staged rollout state machines with automatic halt and rollback on health signals
A/B partitioning and idempotent update protocols under arbitrary interruption
milestones: Build a device emulator with configurable connectivity drop rates, battery drain and boot outcomes
Implement chunked firmware delivery that resumes from the last verified chunk after disconnects
Add A/B partition logic on the device with boot-health reporting and automatic rollback
Build a rollout controller with cohorts, health gates and a kill switch, and test it with a deliberately bad firmware
Simulate a 'store reopens' herd of 30k devices, then add token-bucket admission and jitter until p99 control-plane latency stays flat
